editorial.headline: Building Indonesia’s Oil and Gas Civil Infrastructure
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the construction and upkeep of the civil works that carry Indonesia’s oil and gas industry across land, underground routes and offshore waters.
editorial.body:
This activity is the civil-infrastructure end of the oil and gas business: building, maintaining and, where needed, rebuilding the physical structures used by both upstream and downstream operations. Its scope reaches above ground, below ground and into the water. Long-distance oil and gas pipelines and offshore platforms sit squarely within that terrain. The defining work is not the extraction or trade of petroleum itself, but the specialised civil construction that makes those activities physically possible.

The registration is open at every stated business scale: micro, small, medium and large. That breadth matters because the activity describes a class of construction work rather than a single project format. A business may be engaged in the development, maintenance or reconstruction of the relevant civil structures, provided its work remains within this oil-and-gas infrastructure scope. The record also identifies the construction sub-classifications ST006 and BS013, anchoring the activity in a clearly defined technical construction category.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In Bali, the picture is also open for PMA registration rather than blocked by the province-wide moratorium. The reason is specific: at the large-business scale, OSS risk is classified as medium-high or high, so the activity is not caught by Bali’s permanent restriction on PMA registrations for low- and medium-low-risk activities. That is a meaningful distinction, not a cosmetic one. A business should still read its actual scale and risk position carefully, but the record’s conclusion is plain: this activity is not barred from PMA registration in Bali under that moratorium.

For founders, the practical reading is straightforward. This is a construction activity for the substantial civil systems behind oil and gas operations, available across the stated scale spectrum and fully open to foreign ownership nationally. Bali does not close the door to PMA registration for it; its large-scale risk position places it outside the moratorium’s blocked categories. The opportunity is therefore defined by technical scope and project capability, not by a Bali-specific PMA prohibition.
